In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have a good understanding of the finite-volume corrections to the two-body scattering amplitudes, which can be used in lattice computations of hadronic weak decays.
we have a good qualitative understanding of the finite size effects in the strong and electromagnetic interactions of hadrons and their implications for lattice QCD.
the lattice calculations have been successful in providing a quantitative understanding of the hadronic weak decays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to establish a rigorous connection between the finite volume spectrum of a two-hadron system and its infinite volume scattering matrix.
the finite volume quantization is an effective way to extract the weak decay constants from lattice data.
the finite volume effects can be systematically controlled in lattice QCD computations of weak hadronic matrix elements.

the lattice spacing dependence of the finite volume corrections to weak decay matrix elements can be computed in perturbation theory.
the two-particle states in a finite volume are described in terms of the scattering amplitudes in infinite volume, which are in turn expressed in terms of the two-particle scattering phase shifts.
